## Bundle scope

This document is rendered by Quarto, transformed by Pandoc, and compiled by
LuaLaTeX. It demonstrates how a chemical engineer can combine consistent
units, reaction notation, equations, tables, process diagrams, control
schematics, molecular structures, reusable terminology, algorithms, and
table-driven scientific plots in one reproducible source system. The values
are illustrative and do not represent experimental or validation data.

::: {#fig-pieces-fit}
```{=latex}
\centering
\input{figures/how-pieces-fit.tex}
```

How the pieces fit: Quarto owns the document workflow while LaTeX packages
provide focused notation and rendering tools.
:::

Quarto is the manager rather than another competing typesetting layer
[@quarto2026]. TikZ and PGFPlots remain inspectable LaTeX sources
[@tikz2026; @pgfplots2026].

## Scientific notation that stays consistent

The material balance for species $A$ in a constant-volume
\gls{cstr} can be written with `derivative`, `mathtools`, and
`unicode-math` as

```{=latex}
\begin{equation}
  V\pdv{C_A}{t}=F(C_{A,0}-C_A)-VkC_A,
  \qquad
  \symbf{N}\,\symbf{r}=\symbf{0}.
\end{equation}
```

`siunitx` owns values, uncertainty, ranges, and numeric alignment:

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\begin{threeparttable}
\caption{Illustrative operating conditions.}
\begin{tabular}{@{}l S[table-format=3.2] l@{}}
\toprule
Quantity & {Value} & {Unit} \\
\midrule
Temperature & 355.20 & \si{\kelvin} \\
Pressure & 4.70 & \si{\barunit} \\
Molar flow & 12.20 & \si{\kmol\per\hour} \\
Heat duty & -48.3 & \si{\kilo\watt} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\begin{tablenotes}[flushleft]\footnotesize
\item Values demonstrate formatting only. A project table must record its source and basis.
\end{tablenotes}
\end{threeparttable}
\end{center}
```

`mhchem` handles formulas and reactions:
$\ce{CO2(aq) + 2 RNH2 <=> RNHCOO- + RNH3+}$.
`chemnum` supplies stable compound identifiers such as solvent
\cmpd{solvent} and product \cmpd{product}. In teaching material, `cancel`
can expose an assumption without changing the governing equation:
$\cancel{\pdv{C_A}{t}}=0$ at steady state.

```{=latex}
\begin{assumption}[Ideal illustrative reactor]
The gallery neglects axial dispersion and heat loss. This assumption is a
typesetting example, not a claim about a physical plant.
\end{assumption}
```

## Matrix and table tools

`nicematrix` makes block structure visible in a Jacobian while keeping the
mathematics editable:

```{=latex}
\[
\begin{bNiceMatrix}[first-row,first-col]
  & C_A & T & P \\
f_A & -F/V-k & -C_A\pdv{k}{T} & 0 \\
f_T & -\Delta H\,k & -UA/(\rho C_pV) & 0 \\
f_P & 0 & 0 & 1 \\
\CodeAfter
  \SubMatrix[{1-1}{2-2}]
\end{bNiceMatrix}
\]
```

The same retained CSV can feed both a table and a plot. `pgfplotstable`
formats the data without recomputing it:

```{=latex}
\begin{center}
\pgfplotstabletypeset[
  col sep=comma,
  columns={volume,model,observation,lower,upper},
  every head row/.style={before row=\toprule,after row=\midrule},
  every last row/.style={after row=\bottomrule},
  columns/volume/.style={
    column name={\multicolumn{1}{c}{Volume / \si{\meter\cubed}}},
    column type={S[table-format=1.1]},string type
  },
  columns/model/.style={
    column name={\multicolumn{1}{c}{Model}},
    column type={S[table-format=1.2]},string type
  },
  columns/observation/.style={
    column name={\multicolumn{1}{c}{Observation}},
    column type={S[table-format=1.2]},string type
  },
  columns/lower/.style={
    column name={\multicolumn{1}{c}{Lower}},
    column type={S[table-format=1.2]},string type
  },
  columns/upper/.style={
    column name={\multicolumn{1}{c}{Upper}},
    column type={S[table-format=1.2]},string type
  }
]{data/reactor-profile.csv}
\end{center}
```

Use `longtable`, `multirow`, `makecell`, `csvsimple`, and `pdflscape` when the
content truly needs continued pages, row groups, multiline headers, CSV row
selection, or landscape orientation. They are not reasons to make every table
complicated.

## TikZ as the semantic diagram layer

::: {#fig-tikz-gallery}
```{=latex}
\centering
\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\input{figures/tikz-tool-gallery.tex}}
```

The core libraries provide relative placement, matrices, calculated geometry,
intersections, semantic shapes, fitted regions, background layers, and modern
arrows. `tikz-ext` adds multi-node positioning, orthogonal routing, node-family
sizing, convenient layers, path arrows, true arc-to operations, arcs through a
point, and controlled whole-picture sizing when those gaps are real.
:::

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

::: {#fig-tikz-ext-gallery}
```{=latex}
\centering
\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{\input{figures/tikz-ext-gallery.tex}}
```

Four independent subfigures keep unrelated demonstrations in separate
coordinate systems: (a) relative positioning and shared node dimensions,
(b) orthogonal signal routing and layers, (c) path operations, and (d) the
scaling role.
`ext.topaths.arcthrough` and
`ext.scalepicture` remain conditional APIs: the installed files load, but their
advertised path/key syntax does not execute under this 2026 toolchain.
:::

```{=latex}
\FloatBarrier
```

`tikzmark` connects prose to a diagram without converting the sentence to an
image. Here the \tikzmarknode{balance-anchor}{mass balance} is a named anchor.

```{=latex}
\begin{tikzpicture}[remember picture,overlay]
  \node[cse note,anchor=north] (balance-note)
    at ([yshift=-8mm]balance-anchor.south) {named prose anchor};
  \draw[-Latex,cseOrange,thick]
    (balance-note.north) -- ([yshift=-1mm]balance-anchor.south);
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Algorithms, code, callouts, and lists

```{=latex}
\begin{tcolorbox}[csebox,title={A useful engineering callout}]
A nonlinear solver success flag is not physical acceptance. Check residuals,
conservation, bounds, phase identity, and sensitivity to initialization.
\end{tcolorbox}

\begin{algorithmic}[1]
\Require Feed state, specifications, tolerances
\State Normalize composition and verify units
\State Solve material and energy balances
\If{residuals and physical acceptance tests pass}
  \State retain the state and diagnostics
\Else
  \State report the failure class
\EndIf
\end{algorithmic}
```

Raw LaTeX can use `listings`; Quarto normally owns fenced-code highlighting:

```python
def conversion(c_in, c_out):
    if c_in <= 0:
        raise ValueError("inlet concentration must be positive")
    return (c_in - c_out) / c_in
```

`enumitem` is appropriate when an author-controlled article needs deliberate
list spacing. Beamer keeps ownership of slide lists.

## Layout and visual QA defaults

1. design shared figures at the smallest article or Beamer placement;
2. anchor labels so they grow away from paths and page edges;
3. place panel captions below a named bounding box with an explicit gutter;
4. route connectors separately from nodes and prose, and isolate unrelated path demonstrations;
5. render every final page and inspect it at full size;
6. keep figures inside semantic sections with `\FloatBarrier` where needed;
7. use contact sheets for flow, not as the only overlap check.

`chktex`, `lacheck`, and `texfot` are useful source and log checks, but raster
inspection remains the acceptance test for overlap, clipping, and legibility.
See `references/latex-layout-and-qa.md` for the release sequence.

## Package profiles

Load only the packages required by the selected output profile. The table names
the default owner for each role and incompatible alternatives:

| Role | Use here or add when triggered | Do not combine by default |
|---|---|---|
| Fonts and math | `fontspec`, `unicode-math`, `mathtools`, `derivative`, `microtype` | `bm` belongs to a traditional math-font profile |
| Chemistry | `mhchem`, `chemfig`, `chemnum` | `chemmacros` replaces the chemistry syntax when its wider model is required |
| Tables | `booktabs`, `siunitx`, `threeparttable`, `pgfplotstable`; conditional `longtable`, `multirow`, `makecell`, `csvsimple`, `pdflscape` | `tabularray` is a complete alternative table system |
| Terms | `glossaries-extra` | `acro` is the acronym-only alternative |
| Code | Quarto highlighting; `listings` for raw LaTeX | `minted` only with a trusted source and resolved external highlighter |
| Algorithms | `algorithmicx` + `algpseudocode` | `algorithm2e` is a complete replacement |
| Document structure | `subfiles`, `import`, `xr-hyper`, `pdfpages` when the project shape requires them | Keep a flat source tree until scale proves otherwise |
| Identity and links | Quarto links plus `xurl`; conditional `orcidlink` | Let venue classes own their hyperlink stack |
| Draft/review | Git + `latexdiff`; conditional `lineno`, `changes`, `todonotes` | Remove draft markup from final output |
| Beamer | Moloch, `appendixnumberbeamer`; conditional `pdfpc`, tested-viewer `animate` | Beamer owns geometry, navigation, colors, and lists |
| External media | `graphicx`; conditional `svg` with a controlled Inkscape route | Prefer a committed PDF for portable publication builds |

`standalone` is the reuse boundary for a TikZ or PGFPlots figure that must
compile independently. `adjustbox` can constrain reviewed content, but it
must not hide unreadable design. TikZ `external` is a measured performance
mode, not a default; its controlled build owns the cache. `tikzscale`,
`tikzplotlib`, `gnuplottex`, novelty diagram packages, and direct shell calls
remain outside the selected bundle because the native sources already cover
the intended jobs.

## Quarto templates for real projects

The article profile keeps stable packages in `tex/article-preamble.tex`:

```yaml
format:
  pdf:
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    keep-tex: true
    include-in-header:
      - tex/article-preamble.tex
```

The Beamer profile uses a smaller header and lets the class own slide layout:

```yaml
format:
  beamer:
    pdf-engine: lualatex
    theme: moloch
    aspectratio: 169
    include-in-header:
      - tex/beamer-preamble.tex
```

Inspect generated TeX when package order or a Pandoc transformation is
uncertain. Keep scientific calculations outside TeX and feed retained values
to the document layer.
